summary_paraphrase: Wordless. A boy kept awake by a dripping yard tap tells his grandmother in the morning; his own attempt to close it fails, she calls a man with a toolbox who mends it and praises the boy, and that night he sleeps while the dry tap shines outside.

characters.name: Zuko
characters.desire: (inferred) to stop the dripping so he can sleep and stop the waste
characters.change: from sleepless and troubled to praised and asleep

characters.name: (unnamed man with a toolbox)
characters.relation_to_protagonist: repairer called in; praises Zuko and lets him help

humor_notes: Little humour; background creatures (snail, ladybird, bee, butterfly, caterpillar) recur on outdoor spreads as a quiet find-me layer.

repetition.description: opening and closing in the same night bedroom; the window detail changes from dripping tap to shining dry tap
repetition.why: a circular frame makes the change visible in one detail and ends the day on sleep

repetition.description: the same yard composition (tap left, house right, Zuko and grandmother on the path) recurs while the puddles shrink to none
repetition.why: a fixed stage lets a pre-reader spot what changed: puddles, drips, who is at the tap

repetition.description: small creatures (snail, ladybird, bee, butterfly) appear on each outdoor spread
repetition.why: invites pointing and searching; whether children use it is not observed

notes: Wordless: every page's information is in the picture.
Night spreads are indigo and closed-in; day spreads open to a bright sky: light marks the problem and its end.
The single bird's-eye view (p7) is reserved for the moment of effort.
The thought cloud (p3) is the only device that shows an inner state.
The 'crying' of the title is drawn as tear-shaped drops; the sound in Book Dash's blurb is never written.

strengths: a small, real household problem a young child can notice
circular night-to-night frame ends on sleep
the child notices and reports; an adult acknowledges him and lets him take part in the fix
a recurring stage makes change easy to spot without words
weaknesses: the fix comes from adults; the child's own attempt fails and he is away at school during the repair
the motion lines on the first spread are ambiguous (tiredness or noise) without the blurb
grandmother's pointing on p6 can read as scolding or as an instruction

anti_patterns.note: mild: repair is an adult job by design, and the child is credited (p10-11)

child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: Everyday household problem; nothing frightening. Wordless, so an adult narrates.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
